primary_frame: Regression: explain employee performance_rating from workplace and demographic attributes
alternative_frames: Classification: predict salary_band from employee attributes
Exploratory: identify clusters of employee work profiles
Regression: predict satisfaction_score from work conditions and demographics
required_checks: Test pairwise correlations between all numeric features and performance_rating for statistical significance
Check whether salary_band levels show any systematic relationship with numeric features
Assess performance_rating distribution for normality and detect potential synthetic data signatures
Test for multicollinearity among candidate predictor variables
Fit a baseline regression model and evaluate R-squared to confirm whether predictive signal exists
Run a permutation or shuffle test to distinguish real signal from noise-level associations
framing_risks: No target variable is specified; performance_rating is assumed based on column semantics
Feature distributions and lack of logical feature-target relationships suggest data may be purely synthetic noise with no recoverable signal
Salary band levels appear unordered relative to experience or other features, undermining classification framing
With 800 rows and 9 features, spurious correlations may reach marginal significance even in random data
Absence of domain context makes it impossible to distinguish causal from correlational interpretations
